title: Minimize Result by Adding Parentheses to Expression
summary: Given a string expression in the form "+" where and are positive integers, add a pair of parentheses to make the expression valid and evaluate to the smallest possible value.
statement: Given a string expression in the form "+" where and are positive integers, add a pair of parentheses to make the expression valid and evaluate to the smallest possible value. The left parenthesis must precede the '+' and the right parenthesis must follow it. Return the modified expression. If multiple answers yield the same result, any valid answer is acceptable. The expression values before and after adding parentheses will fit within a signed 32-bit integer.
constraints: expression contains two positive decimal integers separated by one plus sign.
Insert one pair of parentheses enclosing the plus sign; adjacent outside digits multiply the parenthesized sum.
Return the expression with minimum evaluated value.
hints: Each valid answer is determined by one cut in each operand.
Enumerate the left start and right end of the parenthesized addition.
Treat an absent outside factor as one, evaluate, and retain the first minimum string.
The two nested loops visit every legal parentheses placement exactly once.
editorial: The two nested loops visit every legal parentheses placement exactly once.

tests.explanation: Choosing 2(47+38) gives 170, the minimum over every left/right split.
The minimum placement is 1(2+3)4, which evaluates to twenty.
